answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must maintain a private continuous computation that produces a unique non-transferable relic every epoch. This relic is bridged into a public verification canyon where peers challenge its sequential integrity. An attacker forging many identities must run separate long-lived processes on distinct hardware for each, because the relic's sequential dependency prevents parallelization or cheap cloning; the real cost is continuous dedicated compute and storage per fake, not just a one-time key generation.
